description:
RuntimeDemandWalk::demand_table (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:131) makes a ValueMap sized to the whole body per ask: value_map.rs:38 from runtime_demand.rs:132 is about 3,600 tables and most of 9.3 MB, via runtime_demand.rs:1416 and :1369.

Change: read who keeps each table and who drops it. Tables that are dropped after one use come from a pool the walk owns, or the caller's table is cleared and reused; tables that are stored are sized to what they hold if they are sparse.

Evidence: census of the OptionParser probe at c0e52fbaf (tip of #518; 734,597 allocations): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/464fcf92-8f92-4767-a8fb-4e4eea4b6d45/scratchpad/census/c0e52fbaf_top.txt; call chains: cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/464fcf92-8f92-4767-a8fb-4e4eea4b6d45/scratchpad/census && python3 chain.py c0e52fbaf.pkl <file:line> <depth> "" <n>; line numbers are exact at commit c0e52fbaf.

Signal: full gate green; no golden or pin moves except a falling pin, which is lowered and listed; program output and canonical backend dump identical on the probe; allocation count before and after in the commit.
title: Runtime-demand walks reuse their value tables
